name: Rex Medical
old_description: from the peripheral arteries in patients with occlusive atherosclerotic disease.
about:
Rex Medical is headquartered in Conshohocken, Pennsylvania. The company specializes in the development, manufacturing, and marketing of innovative, minimally invasive medical devices. It targets the cardiovascular, venous access, endosurgery, and oncology markets with products designed to address unmet clinical needs.

The REVOLUTION™ Peripheral Atherectomy System is Rex Medical's flagship device, intended to treat occlusive atherosclerotic disease in peripheral arteries by breaking apart and removing plaque. The company manages the entire product lifecycle in-house, from design and development through manufacturing and commercialization.

Rex Medical serves hospitals, clinics, and medical device distributors across the cardiovascular, venous access, endosurgery, and oncology sectors. Its devices are used in minimally invasive procedures that aim to improve patient outcomes and deliver high-quality care.

The company maintains ISO 13485 certification for its quality management system and states that its mission is to improve patient outcomes through innovation in technology. Rex Medical emphasizes addressing unmet clinical needs with minimally invasive solutions.

name: Rheem Water Manufacturing Facility
old_description: Rheem specializes in dependable, quiet, efficient systems that make your home comfortable.
about:
Rheem Manufacturing Company operates a major production facility in Montgomery, Alabama. The company traces its origins back a century, evolving from early steel drum manufacturing into a global supplier of air and water comfort systems. While the exact founding year and ownership structure are not publicly detailed on its website, Rheem describes itself as a family of more than 50 brands serving markets worldwide.

The Montgomery facility and related operations produce a broad range of residential and commercial equipment, including tank and tankless water heaters, heat pump water heaters, boilers, air conditioners, furnaces, heat pumps, and indoor air quality systems. Product lines such as the Endeavor® heating and cooling series, Maximus™ water heater, ProTerra® heat pump water heaters, and Triton® gas water heaters are engineered at scale for both homeowner and commercial applications. The company also provides digital tools like BIM/CAD and Revit files for specification support.

Rheem serves homeowners, commercial building owners, and the contractor/plumber/installer network through its Pro Partner Programs. Its products are specified in residential construction, commercial building projects, HVAC replacement, and plumbing installations across the Americas, Asia-Pacific, and the Middle East.

The company emphasizes a sustainability mandate that targets a 30 percent reduction in emissions intensity across product lifecycles. It positions its century of manufacturing expertise and single-source product portfolio as differentiators for customers seeking integrated comfort solutions.

name: Rhino Meat Processing
old_description: Heart of Dakota Packing and Wollman Ranch are not licensed meat processing establishments
about:
Rhino Meat Processing LLC operates from Maddock, North Dakota, where it runs a federally inspected slaughter and processing facility. The company appears in the North Dakota Department of Agriculture’s directory of licensed meat processors under the Federal Slaughter category.

As a federal slaughter establishment, the plant slaughters livestock and processes meat products under continuous USDA inspection. Its products bear the USDA mark of inspection, allowing them to be sold across state lines and exported. The facility may also offer custom-exempt slaughter and processing services for producers who retain ownership of the animals, though those products are labeled “Not For Sale” and cannot enter commercial channels.

The business serves wholesale distributors, retailers, and export markets that require federally inspected meat. It also works with livestock producers seeking custom processing for personal use. The directory does not list specific brand names or customer accounts beyond the facility’s regulatory classification.

The company’s federal inspection status is its primary differentiator, granting access to interstate and international markets that state-inspected plants cannot reach. No founding date, ownership structure, or specialized equipment details are disclosed in the public listing.

Rhody Tees operates from Cranston, Rhode Island, where founder J.C. Castellanos established the business after accumulating more than 25 years of experience in the graphic industry. The shop provides screen printing, direct-to-film (DTF) transfers, and embroidery for apparel including t-shirts, sweatshirts, polos, hats, and bags, sourcing blanks from over 100 brands. It also runs a large-format printing operation producing signs, banners, yard signs, decals, and see-through vinyl, plus a promotional-products line covering business cards, flyers, and mugs. No facility size, headcount, or annual volume figures are disclosed.

Customers range from small businesses and sports teams to event organizers. Testimonials cite a pet-sitting service, an inflatable-rental company, and individual families needing quick turnaround on custom shirts. The company positions itself as a local partner for any group needing branded wear or marketing materials.

Castellanos states the business was built on close collaboration, unique design, high-quality prints, and reliable on-time delivery, with the philosophy that helping clients grow drives the company's own growth.

name: Rigid Industries LED Lighting
old_description: For the best experience on our site, be sure to turn on Javascript in your browser.
about:
Rigid Industries LED Lighting operates from Gilbert, Arizona, as a limited liability company. The firm designs and builds off-road LED lighting systems for trucks, utility vehicles, and powersports applications.

The product line includes light bars, pods, fog lights, rear-facing lights, street-legal options, scene lighting, and mounting kits. A flagship system called Phoenix offers five selectable color modes ranging from cool white to amber, three power levels, and interchangeable Spot, Drive, and Combo lenses. The company cites patented optic technology and says its lights are tested to meet stringent OEM durability standards.

Customers range from recreational off-roaders to professional racers; top competitors in the Baja 1000 and Mint 400 rely on Rigid lights. The brand also serves the overlanding community through events such as The Big Thing at XOverland Ranch in Montana, and it supplies components that undergo OEM-level validation.

Rigid emphasizes durability as its core differentiator, pointing to a 15-year-old “Torture Test” program that deliberately destroys lights on camera to prove resilience. The combination of adjustable output, swappable optics, and proven race performance is positioned as the reason the company was started and why it continues to lead in the segment.

name: Rising Sun Solar Outfitters
old_description: Designing and installing RV and off-grid solar systems based on your goals and budget
about:
Rising Sun Solar Outfitters operates from Avon, Indiana. The family-owned business traces its roots to the founders' purchase of their first RV, which sparked a passion for renewable energy that grew into a full-time venture. The family now lives the lifestyle they serve — camping in a solar-powered fifth wheel and powering their own home off-grid.

The company designs and installs custom solar systems for recreational vehicles and off-grid properties. Services include system design, installation, consultations, and detailed quotes. Each project is tailored to the customer's specific goals and budget, with an emphasis on safety and reliability. No facility size, headcount, or production volumes are disclosed.

Primary customers are RV owners seeking mobile power freedom, owners of remote cabins or off-grid homes, and homeowners looking to reduce utility dependence. The company serves the RV/mobile market, off-grid residential sector, and broader renewable energy space, with concrete examples including Harvest Hosts and Boondockers Welcome overnight stays, cabin generator replacement, and whole-home off-grid conversions.

The business was born from firsthand experience: the founders wanted to run appliances silently while boondocking, keep food cold without generator noise, and maximize time away from hookups. That personal need drives their approach — they build systems they would trust for their own family's comfort and independence.
